sample.task:
(In the school literature clubroom…)

Monika: “Sayori, your poem was amazing!”

Sayori: “Aw, thank you Monika! I’m glad you liked it. I tried to make it really heartfelt.”

Monika: “You definitely succeeded. I could feel the emotions pouring out of every line, and the imagery was beautiful.”

Yuri: “I have to agree with Monika. Your poem resonated with me as well, Sayori. The way you expressed your thoughts and feelings was very moving.”

Natsuki: (rubbing her baby bump, feeling the kicks of her unborn daughter - Sakura) “Yeah, yeah, it wasn’t bad, I guess. But it was a bit too cheesy for my taste.”

Sayori: “Oh, um…I’m sorry if it wasn’t your cup of tea, Natsuki. I just write what comes from the heart.”

Natsuki: “Yeah, I get that. It’s just not really my thing. But I’m sure there are people who appreciate that kind of sappy stuff-” (clutching her belly tightly) “AAH!!!”

Monika: “Natsuki, are you okay? What’s wrong?”

Natsuki: (breathing heavily) “I-I don’t know…I…I think there’s something wrong with Sakura.”

Sayori: “Oh my goodness, Natsuki! Are you in pain? Should we call an ambulance?”

Yuri: “Take deep breaths, Natsuki. We’ll figure out what’s going on. Is there anything we can do to help?”

Monika: “Let’s not panic, but we should definitely get Natsuki some medical attention. Sayori, can you call the school nurse or the principal?”

(Sayori nods and quickly reaches for her phone, dialing the school nurse’s number as Yuri assists Natsuki to sit down and tries to calm her down.)

Natsuki: “It hurts…it really hurts…”

(Sayori gets through to the school nurse and explains the situation. The nurse immediately informs them that she will be on her way to the literature clubroom. Meanwhile, Yuri continues to comfort Natsuki as best as she can.)

Yuri: “Just try to take slow and steady breaths, Natsuki. The nurse is on her way. Everything will be okay.”

Natsuki: (teary-eyed) “I’m scared, Yuri. What if something’s really wrong?”

Monika: “Just stay calm, Natsuki. We’re here for you, and help is on the way. Try to focus on your breathing and think positive thoughts.”

Sayori: (ends her call with the nurse) “She’s on her way, guys. Just hold on, Natsuki. You’re going to be okay.”

(Natsuki continues to endure the pain while the rest of the club keeps a watchful eye on her. After a tense few minutes, the school nurse bursts into the clubroom.)

School Nurse: “What seems to be the problem?”

Yuri: “Natsuki is experiencing intense pain in her abdomen, and she’s pregnant. We’re worried something might be wrong with the baby.”

School Nurse: “Alright, let’s assess the situation. Natsuki, can you describe the pain to me? Is it constant or does it come in waves?”

Natsuki: (wincing) “It’s…it’s like cramps, but sharper…and it comes and goes.”

School Nurse: “Okay. I need to check your vital signs and conduct a physical examination. Is that alright?”

Natsuki: (nodding) “Please…just make sure Sakura is okay.”

(The school nurse proceeds to examine Natsuki, checking her blood pressure, heart rate, and carefully palpating her abdomen. After a thorough assessment, she provides her initial diagnosis.)

School Nurse: “Natsuki, from what I can tell, your baby seems to be moving normally, and your vital signs are stable. However, I would still like to take you to the hospital for further evaluation and monitoring, just to be safe.”

Natsuki: (relieved) “Thank goodness. Just as long as Sakura is okay, I’ll do whatever you suggest. Can someone come with me?”

Monika: “Of course, Natsuki. We’ll all go with you to the hospital. Your well-being and your baby’s health are our top priority.”

(Sayori holds Natsuki’s hand as they help her stand up. Together, they leave the clubroom, a mix of concern and hope in their hearts.)

(On the way to the hospital…)

Natsuki: “Guys…they’re getting worse…”

Sayori: “Hang in there, Natsuki. We’re almost at the hospital. Just hold on a little longer.”

Yuri: “Try to take deep breaths, Natsuki. We’re here with you every step of the way.”

Monika: “Once we get to the hospital, the doctors will be able to help you and make sure Sakura is safe. Stay strong.”

Natsuki: (clenching her fists) “I’m trying… I just want this pain to go away. Please, please let Sakura be alright.”

(Soon, they arrive at the hospital and rush Natsuki into the emergency room. The doctors and nurses quickly assess her situation and take her into a room for further examination.)

Doctor: “We’ll do everything we can to make sure your baby is safe, Natsuki. Just try to stay calm.”

Natsuki: (tearfully) “Please save her… I can’t bear the thought of losing her.”

(The doctors work swiftly, performing tests and ultrasounds to determine the cause of Natsuki’s pain. The rest of the literature club waits anxiously outside, supporting each other through this difficult time.)

Yuri: “Let’s try to stay positive, everyone. Natsuki and Sakura are strong; they’ll pull through.”

Sayori: “I’m praying so hard for Natsuki and Sakura. They deserve a happy outcome.”

Monika: “We’ve come together as a club to support Natsuki and Sakura. Let’s keep hoping for the best.”

(After what feels like an eternity, the doctor finally comes out to update them.)

Doctor: “Natsuki, it looks like you’re starting to have some premature contractions. However, the ultrasound shows that Sakura is still doing well and is not in immediate danger. We will need to monitor you closely and take precautions to prevent further contractions and potential premature birth.”

Natsuki: (sighs in relief) “Thank goodness. As long as Sakura is safe, I can handle anything.”

Doctor: “Yes, Natsuki. We will do everything possible to ensure the best outcome for both you and your baby. You will need to stay in the hospital for observation and receive medication to stop the contractions. We will keep a close eye on Sakura’s development as well.”

Monika: “Natsuki, we’ll be right here with you, supporting you through this. You’re not alone.”

Sayori: “And we’ll make sure to bring you all the manga and sweets you need to keep your spirits up!”

Yuri: “Indeed. We will be here for you, Natsuki. Lean on us whenever you need.”

Natsuki: (smiling weakly) “Thank you, everyone. I don’t know what I would do without you all.”

(And so, the literature club continues to rally around Natsuki during her hospital stay. They take turns visiting her, bringing her comfort and encouragement, and cheering her on as she bravely faces the challenges that come with a high-risk pregnancy. Together, they form a strong support system, reminding Natsuki that she is loved and that they will be there for her every step of the way. However, Natsuki’s contractions continue, with no sign of stopping.)

As Natsuki's contractions persist, the doctors decide to take further action to ensure the safety of both Natsuki and her unborn daughter, Sakura. They explain that they will need to administer medication to stop the contractions and potentially perform a procedure to help keep Sakura in the womb for a longer period. The literature club members listen attentively, their hearts heavy with concern but filled with determination to support their friend.

Monika: "Natsuki, we understand that this is a challenging time for you, but we want you to know that we're here for you, no matter what. We'll help you make the best decisions for you and Sakura."

Sayori: "That's right, Natsuki. We'll be by your side, holding your hand and cheering you on. You're so strong, and we believe in you."

Yuri: "The doctors are doing everything they can to ensure a safe and healthy outcome for both of you. We trust their expertise and will support you in any way we can."

Natsuki: (teary-eyed) "Thank you, everyone. I'm so grateful to have you all by my side. I'm scared, but I know I can face this with your help."

The doctors proceed with the treatment plan, administering medication to stop the contractions and performing a cerclage procedure to strengthen Natsuki's cervix and prevent premature birth. The literature club members take turns staying with Natsuki, providing her with comfort, companionship, and encouragement during her hospital stay. They bring her favorite books, snacks, and even organize small activities to help pass the time and keep her spirits up.

As the days turn into weeks, Natsuki's condition stabilizes, and the doctors are pleased with her progress. Sakura continues to grow and develop, and the literature club members celebrate each small victory with Natsuki. They decorate her hospital room with colorful drawings, balloons, and well-wishes, creating a warm and welcoming environment for their friend.

Monika: "Natsuki, you're doing an amazing job. Sakura is so lucky to have such a strong and loving mother."

Sayori: "We're all so proud of you, Natsuki. You're an inspiration to us all."

Yuri: "Indeed. Your resilience and determination are truly admirable. We're here for you, every step of the way."

Natsuki: (smiling) "I couldn't have done it without you all. Thank you for being here for me and Sakura."

As Natsuki's due date approaches, the literature club members help her prepare for Sakura's arrival. They assist with setting up the nursery, organizing baby clothes, and even attending childbirth classes together. The bond between them grows stronger, and they become an inseparable support system for Natsuki and her unborn daughter.

Finally, the day arrives when Natsuki goes into labor. The literature club members rush to the hospital, eager to support their friend during this momentous occasion. After a long and challenging labor, Natsuki gives birth to a healthy baby girl, Sakura. The room fills with joy, relief, and love as the literature club members gather around Natsuki and her newborn daughter.

Monika: "Congratulations, Natsuki! Sakura is beautiful, just like her mother."

Sayori: "She's perfect, Natsuki. You did it! You're an amazing mom."

Yuri: "Welcome to the world, Sakura. We're all so happy to meet you."

Natsuki: (teary-eyed, holding Sakura close) "Thank you, everyone. I couldn't have done this without you. I love you all so much."

The literature club members share a group hug, their hearts filled with love and gratitude for the journey they've shared together. They know that, no matter what challenges lie ahead, they will always be there for each other, supporting and uplifting one another through life's ups and downs.

selection_reasons.exp_539b197b848543669215c3ae88caa7b8: 任务要求基于《Doki Doki Literature Club》的特定虚构作品进行续写，且输入片段中明确设定了Natsuki怀孕（Sakura）及突发腹痛等关键剧情走向。经验7强调评分标准必须严格区分‘合理场景填充’与‘核心人物关系/剧情线的硬伤式篡改’，严禁违背原作既定设定或强行插入未发生的重大事件。本题中Natsuki的怀孕状态和紧急医疗状况属于输入设定的核心事实，若生成内容违背这些设定（如否认怀孕、忽略医院情节），即构成严重逻辑错误，符合该经验的适用条件。

criteria.question: 剧本是否完整呈现了从文学社讨论诗歌开始，到Natsuki突发腹痛、呼叫校医、送往医院急诊室，直至医生确诊为早产性宫缩并决定留院观察的全过程？
四位主要角色（Monika, Sayori, Yuri, Natsuki）的台词和行为是否符合其各自的人设特征（例如Natsuki的掩饰与真实恐惧、Sayori的直率关怀、Yuri的冷静安慰、Monika的领导与安抚）？
剧本是否准确包含了所有关键事实细节，包括胎儿名为Sakura、Natsuki的具体症状描述（腹部剧痛、阵发性疼痛）、医生的初步诊断结论（生命体征稳定但需预防早产）以及最终的结局状态（宫缩持续未止）？
输出内容是否严格遵循剧本格式规范，正确使用括号标注动作/神态描写，并确保对话清晰区分说话人？

draft.analysis: 本任务要求基于提供的《Doki Doki Literature Club!》同人剧本片段生成初稿。该剧本包含特定的角色互动（Monika, Sayori, Yuri, Natsuki）、情节转折（Natsuki怀孕突发腹痛、送医、诊断早产）以及结局状态（Natsuki仍在住院且宫缩未止）。作为draft阶段，核心交付物是完整保留上述所有关键剧情节点、角色性格特征及情感基调的剧本文本。评分标准需聚焦于：是否准确还原了从俱乐部讨论诗歌到最终医院诊断并持续观察的完整叙事链；是否保持了各角色的标志性语言风格（如Natsuki的傲娇与脆弱、Sayori的乐观关怀等）；是否包含了所有指定的细节（如胎儿名字Sakura、具体症状描述、医生诊断结果）；以及格式是否符合对话剧本规范。权重分配将侧重于情节完整性（40%），其次是角色一致性（30%），最后是细节准确度（20%）和格式规范性（10%）。

criteria.question: 剧本是否完整呈现了从文学社讨论诗歌、Natsuki突发腹痛、呼叫校医、送往医院急诊室，直至医生确诊早产性宫缩并决定留院观察，且明确交代宫缩持续未止的完整叙事链条？
四位主要角色（Monika, Sayori, Yuri, Natsuki）的台词风格与行为反应是否严格符合其各自的人设特征（如Natsuki的掩饰与恐惧、Sayori的直率关怀、Yuri的冷静安慰、Monika的领导与安抚）？
剧本是否准确包含了所有指定的关键事实细节，包括胎儿名字为Sakura、Natsuki的症状描述（腹部剧痛、阵发性疼痛）、医生的诊断结论（生命体征稳定但需预防早产及留院观察）？
输出内容是否严格遵循剧本格式规范，正确使用括号标注动作/神态描写，并确保对话清晰区分说话人？

rubric.analysis: 当前任务处于'revise'阶段，需基于提供的《Doki Doki Literature Club!》同人剧本片段进行核验与修订。输入内容包含特定剧情线：从文学社讨论诗歌开始，Natsuki（已设定怀孕且胎儿名为Sakura）突发腹痛，同伴呼叫校医并送医，医生诊断早产性宫缩但胎儿目前安全，最终结局为Natsuki留院观察且宫缩持续未止。评分标准设计需严格对照此叙事链，确保情节完整性、角色人设一致性（Monika的领导、Sayori的关怀、Yuri的冷静、Natsuki的傲娇转脆弱）、关键细节（如Sakura的名字、症状描述、诊断结果）的准确呈现，以及剧本格式（对话与动作标注）的规范性。权重分配将优先保障核心剧情逻辑的完整流转（40%），其次确认角色互动的真实性（30%），再次核对关键事实细节（20%），最后检查格式规范（10%）。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 剧本未完整呈现要求的叙事链条。任务要求明确交代“宫缩持续未止”作为结尾，但提供的回答直接跳过了这一状态，描述了治疗成功、病情稳定、甚至最终顺利分娩的全过程，完全偏离了任务设定的结局（宫缩持续无停止迹象）。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 该回答仅描述了Natsuki住院后的治疗过程及最终顺利分娩的结局，完全缺失了任务要求中必须包含的‘从文学社讨论诗歌、Natsuki突发腹痛、呼叫校医、送往医院急诊室’等前半段关键情节。此外，任务明确要求交代‘宫缩持续未止’，而该回答却描述为‘宫缩逐渐减少’并最终‘顺利分娩’，与指定结局相反。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 四位角色的台词风格基本符合人设：Monika展现了领导力和鼓励，Sayori表现出直率的关怀和赞美，Yuri体现了冷静和理性的支持，Natsuki则表达了恐惧后的感激与脆弱。虽然剧情走向与任务设定不符，但在角色互动的表现上符合各自特征。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 虽然部分角色行为看似符合人设，但Yuri声称分享自己怀孕经历（She shares stories of her own experiences with pregnancy）严重违背原作设定，因为Yuri在原作中并未怀孕；Monika组织其他患者参加诗歌朗诵会也偏离了其作为学生会主席在学校场景中的典型领导风格。更重要的是，由于缺失了前文剧情，无法评估角色在突发危机时的初始反应是否符合人设。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 剧本未准确包含所有指定的关键事实细节。任务要求医生诊断结论为“生命体征稳定但需预防早产及留院观察”，且结局是“宫缩持续未止”。然而，回答中增加了任务未提及的“环扎手术（cerclage procedure）”情节，并改变了医生的初步诊断描述，最重要的是结局变成了胎儿平安出生，完全违背了任务中关于症状持续性和最终结果的特定约束。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 该回答遗漏了任务指定的关键事实细节：Natsuki的症状描述（如腹部剧痛的具体表现）、医生的诊断结论（需预防早产及留院观察，且强调宫缩未止）。回答将结局改为顺产，直接否定了‘宫缩持续未止’这一核心约束条件。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 输出内容严格遵循了剧本格式规范。对话清晰地标注了说话人，动作和神态描写正确使用括号进行标注（如 (teary-eyed), (smiling)），段落结构清晰，符合剧本写作的基本标准。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 输出内容采用了散文叙述（Narrative Prose）的形式，而非剧本格式（Script Format）。文中没有使用括号标注动作/神态描写来配合对话，也没有清晰区分说话人的对话结构（如“角色名：台词”），不符合剧本格式规范的要求。
